title: August 2026 fresh-intake production - batch H3A (legal, institutional and documentary root asks: the International Seabed Authority, ITLOS, and the IOPP Supplement Form A / Form B)
note: SEVEN ROOTS EXAMINED, THREE CARDS WRITTEN, THREE ALREADY ANSWERED, ONE HELD. The batch was scoped as seven legal/institutional/documentary families and the first job was to find out how many actually needed a card. Three did not. AUG-0095/0096 Freedom of navigation is answered by QB1_A#q19, which carries EEZ Art. 58 and high seas Art. 87 by name alongside transit passage and straits used for international navigation, with innocent passage separated into its own card at QB1_A#q21 - which is exactly the distinction that must not be blurred. The ROOT was correctly dispositioned; the LIMB (AUG-0096, 'condition of freedom of navigation') was NOT answered anywhere in the bank, and is fixed by CORR-UNCLOS-FREEDOM-20260831. AUG-0140 'where to find crew entitlements onboard' is answered by QB9_H#q10, which carries the Seafarer Employment Agreement under Std A2.1 - an individual signed agreement, a copy carried onboard and available to PSC in English, with Std A2.2 wage accounts. QB4_A#q14 is the sibling, not the target: DMLC Part I states national law and Part II states company procedure, and neither is where a seafarer's own entitlements live. This batch first named q14 and the review corrected it. AUG-0148 'what is the grain loading booklet' is answered by QB2_A#q11, which states that the Document of Authorisation is invalid without an approved Grain Stability Booklet and describes what the booklet contains - and which H2 corrected six days ago to carry the third loading configuration. Each of those three was decided by READING THE CARD, not by matching its title: the ORAL-AUG-3 review had just shown that title-only rejection commissions duplicate answers, and the same failure inverted would have produced three duplicates here. AUG-0163 ORB WAS HELD, AND THE HOLD IS WHY THE ANSWER WAS FOUND (see the review section below, which supersedes this paragraph's conclusion). The bank genuinely has no Oil Record Book card and the ask - 'ORB: in detail about the codes' - is a real gap. The local corpus holds the Revised Annex I (MEPC.117(52)) with Appendix III in full: Part I sections A to I, Part II sections A to R. But a widely repeated secondary claim attributes a 2016/2018 revision of the ORB entry codes to MEPC.276(70), and obtaining that resolution showed it amends appendix II Form B ONLY. MEPC.277(70) turned out to be Annex V and MEPC.316(74) Annex VI. So at the time of the hold a later ORB amendment probably existed, was not identified, and was not held - which meant the A-to-I list could not be published as current. Shipping it would have been the BMP5 defect again: an authoritative base that is out of date for the one provision being taught. Held under RQ-A1 rather than shipped - and the reviewer then FOUND the resolution, MEPC.187(59), which is now acquired and filed. RQ-A1 is closed. LOCAL CORPUS FIRST, AND IT WORKED. The Form A / Form B card required NO web research for its substance: the allocation rule is quoted from the Notes to both forms in Appendix II of MEPC.117(52), already held in the shared desktop corpus with a full text layer. The currentness check went outside and returned MEPC.276(70), now preserved in that same corpus. That check was NOT good enough and the review proved it: MEPC.359(79) amends the same appendix and was already on disk, hidden behind a mis-scoped summary row in the corpus's own log. The corpus record and the card are both corrected, and MEPC.187(59) is filed alongside them - three gaps the corpus did not know it had. EXAMINER ATTRIBUTION. All three asks are PANEL_LEVEL_ONLY. No examiner name was added; relationships stay at 958 and examiners at 7. ---- INDEPENDENT REVIEW, AND IT CHANGED THE BATCH ---- A clean-context reviewer returned REVISE on two of the three cards and on two of the four dispositions, and every finding was re-verified by the producer at source before any fix was applied. (1) The Form A/B card's currentness section was WRONG. It named MEPC.276(70) alone and told the candidate the Supplement was last amended in 2018. It was 2024: MEPC.359(79) also amends Appendix II, Form B, replacing the title of section 5 - and that resolution was ALREADY ON DISK in the same folder the batch searched, mis-summarised in the corpus's own instrument log as a reception-facilities amendment. The batch read the log's summary row instead of opening the resolution, which is precisely the failure this repository's own SKILL.md section 8.2c warns about. Both the card and the corpus log are corrected. Form A's own last amendment is 2011, by MEPC.187(59). (2) The ITLOS card said its prompt-release and provisional-measures jurisdiction is 'compulsory whatever else the parties chose'. Article 292(1) and Article 290(5), read verbatim from UN DOALOS, send the question to any tribunal the parties agree on and reach ITLOS only FAILING agreement - within 10 days and two weeks respectively - and Article 292 ends 'unless the parties otherwise agree'. ITLOS is RESIDUAL, not compulsory. The card had correctly attacked the 'everything goes to ITLOS' error under Article 287 and then committed its inverse two paragraphs later. (3) The new ISA card contradicted QB1_A#q19 in the same file on the UNCLOS party count, 172 against 168 - the batch edited that file without checking it. (4) The crew-entitlements disposition named the wrong card: QB4_A#q14 explains DMLC Parts I and II, which are statements of national law and company procedure, whereas QB9_H#q10 carries the Seafarer Employment Agreement under Std A2.1 with the copy carried onboard and available to PSC - which is where a seafarer's entitlements actually live. Re-pointed. (5) AUG-0096, the 'condition of freedom of navigation' limb, was unanswered corpus-wide: 'due regard' returned ZERO hits across all 86 files. Fixed by a bounded correction to q19 under CORR-UNCLOS-FREEDOM-20260831, with trap 56. Smaller findings taken: the reg 2.2 threshold of 200 cubic metres, the Article 20 quotation running over the Tribunal's own gloss, the Article 191 requester limitation, and Article 136's word being 'mankind' where the Authority now writes 'humankind'. ---- AND THE REVIEWER UNBLOCKED THE ORB ---- It identified MEPC.187(59) - adopted 17 July 2009, in force 1 January 2011, amending regulations 1, 12, 13, 17 and 38, Section 3 of BOTH IOPP Supplement forms, and the Oil Record Book Parts I and II. Verified, acquired and filed; RQ-A1 is CLOSED and a new RQ-A2 raised for MEPC.314(74) (electronic record books, in force 1 October 2020), which is not held. AUG-0163 moves from HOLD_CURRENTNESS_UNVERIFIED to QUEUED: the blocker is gone, but the card is NOT authored here because it would ship without the independent review this batch's other cards received.
